guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the transform covers the deck only, not the combat piles
guards.issue: Byrdpip.cs:49-53 collects every ByrdonisEgg from the Deck pile and, `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress)`, ALSO from `Owner.PlayerCombatState.AllCards` -- i.e. a Byrdonis Egg sitting in the draw/hand/discard/exhaust pile of a fight in progress is transformed too. byrdpip.py:25 iterates `run.deck` only. DORMANT for the same reason relic/belt_buckle's AfterObtained is: the sim grants relics through RunState.add_relic between rooms and has no path that obtains a relic inside a combat, and Byrdpip's own grant path is the Byrdonis Egg card's HATCH rest-site option -- a rest site, never a fight. Recorded as a gap rather than a waiver because 'no ported content reaches this' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Porting any mid-combat relic grant makes it live.

guards.what: G3: the pet creature (SummonPet, Byrdpip.cs:69-72, from both AfterObtained and BeforeCombatStart) is not modelled at all
guards.rationale: The port's docstring asserts the pet is pure flavour; the claim is checked here rather than trusted (PROMPT.md bug class 12). It holds, on four independent readings. (a) Monsters/Byrdpip.cs:12-16 gives it MinInitialHp == MaxInitialHp == 9999 and IsHealthBarVisible false; (b) its GenerateMoveStateMachine (:26-31) is a single MoveState 'NOTHING_MOVE' whose body is `Task.CompletedTask` and whose FollowUpState is itself -- no RNG, no effect; (c) it is never targeted, because monster moves aim at CombatState.PlayerCreatures, which filters `c.IsPlayer` (CombatState.cs:75) and a pet creature is not a player, and it is not in `_enemies` so it never takes a turn; (d) the only content that looks the pet up is ByrdSwoop.cs:28, `WithAttackerAnim(..., GetPet<Byrdpip>())` -- the attack animation origin. PlayerCmd.AddPet<T> (PlayerCmd.cs:237-257) draws no RNG either. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT OBSERVABLE: the pet IS in CombatState.Creatures and therefore in CreaturesOnCurrentSide, so it is a participant for BeforeSideTurnStart / AfterTurnStart / AfterBlockCleared. Every ported listener on those hooks filters on `creature == Owner.Creature` or `participants.Contains(...)` (this batch's relic/captains_wheel, relic/candelabra, relic/chandelier and relic/cloak_clasp all do), so no ported effect can see the extra creature -- porting one that reacts to ANY player-side creature without an owner check would. Verdicted deliberate-divergence rather than gap because the observable outcome is identical under every ported reader (binding rule 2). Rule 7: Monsters/Byrdpip.cs, ByrdSwoop.cs, CombatState.cs and PlayerCmd.cs are NOT hashed here.

guards.what: G2: `Skin = new Rng(base.Owner, base.Id).NextItem(SkinOptions)` (Byrdpip.cs:48) and the [SavedProperty] Skin field
guards.rationale: A cosmetic sprite-skin choice with no gameplay reading (its only consumer is Monsters/Byrdpip.cs:18-24 SetupSkins). It is also not an RNG-parity concern, which is why it is checked rather than skipped: `new Rng(owner, id)` CONSTRUCTS a fresh independent generator seeded from the owner and the relic id, so it consumes nothing from any RunRngSet stream. Presentation-only under the shared contract.

PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half (a named RNG stream silently falling back to the shared legacy rng) does NOT apply: TransformTo supplies an explicit replacement, and CardTransformation.GetReplacement returns `Replacement` without touching the Rng when it is set (CardTransformation.cs:55-59). The sim's transform_card only rolls when `into is None` (run.py:437), so both sides consume zero draws. Placement also matches: a Deck-pile transform in C# removes the original and APPENDS the replacement at the end (CardCmd.cs:427-437), which run.transform_card's docstring cites and implements. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardTransformation.cs and run.py are not hashed here.
